title: Automated DLQ Reprocessing
description: Build automated pipelines to inspect, fix, and replay messages from dead-letter queues safely using schedulers, idempotent reprocessing, and audit trails.

data.text: Manual DLQ review does not scale. When dozens or hundreds of messages fail, engineers need an automated pipeline that inspects the payload, applies fixes, and replays the message safely. Automated DLQ processing reduces mean time to recovery while preserving the audit trail and business rules that manual replay often bypasses.

A robust pipeline has four stages: inspect the message for root cause, transform or enrich the payload if needed, replay the message into the main queue, and record the outcome for compliance. Each stage must be idempotent so that replays do not create duplicate side effects.

data.title: Pipeline Stages
items: Inspect: read the message body, headers, and error metadata from the DLQ
Transform: fix known issues such as missing fields, expired tokens, or stale references
Replay: publish the corrected message to the main queue with a unique message ID
Audit: log the replay attempt, outcome, and any manual overrides

data.text: Replaying a message should never create duplicate orders, double-charge a customer, or send the same notification twice. Use idempotency keys stored in a database or cache. If the consumer sees a duplicate key, it skips processing and returns success.

data.title: Replay Without Idempotency Is Dangerous
data.text: If your consumer is not idempotent, automated replay can corrupt data. Always validate idempotency before enabling automated DLQ reprocessing in production.

data.content: An EventBridge rule triggers a Lambda function on a schedule. The Lambda reads up to 10 messages from the DLQ, applies transformations, and sends them back to the main queue.

data.title: Build a Safe DLQ Replay Script
data.description: Write a script or service that reads messages from a DLQ, applies a safe transformation, and publishes them to the main queue with idempotency keys.
steps: Set up a main queue and DLQ in your chosen broker.
Write a producer that intentionally sends 5 malformed messages to trigger the DLQ.
Build a replay consumer that reads from the DLQ.
Add a transformation step that fixes the known issue in the malformed messages.
Publish fixed messages to the main queue with a deduplication key.
Verify the main queue processes the replayed messages without duplicates.
data.expectedOutcome: Malformed messages are automatically repaired and replayed exactly once, with an audit trail showing the replay event.
